fieldValues.title: A forward-reference check against a topological order is vacuous by construction
fieldValues.summary: The forward-reference check must linearise the authored tree — parent before child, siblings by the precedes chain — and use the strongly-connected components of the depends-on graph only as the exemption. Ordering the corpus by a topological sort of the condensation instead would make the check incapable of ever failing: a topological order contains no forward edges by definition.
evidence: check-spec-coherence.mjs check 1 computes Tarjan SCCs over depends-on (44 concepts collapse to 41 components, reproducing #608's three irreducible 2-cycles) and compares against the tree's linearised order
Result on the live corpus: 89 edges, 1 forward (Record -> Field values, allowlisted to #563), 6 backward, 6 within one component, 76 unordered
Edges whose relative order the tree does not yet determine are counted as unordered, never reported as violations
fieldValues.body: The distinction is the whole check. The tree is the constraint — it is what an author wrote and what a reader walks — and the SCC is the exemption that keeps the three genuine cycles from being reported as errors. Swap them and you have a check that passes on any corpus, including one where every concept is used before it is introduced. Related: #608's own 16-forward-reference figure was measured against the rendered reading order, which this check deliberately does not consult, so the two numbers are not comparable and no script reproduces the older one.
